design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (pap_therapy_rentals). Step 0 draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[6,4,4,4]; REFUND (root) takes 6, LABOR, PARTS and SHARE take 4 each.
SCOPE SNAPSHOT. Occupied before: nothing. Claimed by task 0: pap_ext_return_labor, pap_ext_return_parts, pap_ext_used_accessories, pap_ext_self_pay_refund; tools record_return_inspection_bc7317cd (agent) and return_device_for_refund_b6f98fe9 (user). Reserved for task 1 (draw 2 prerequisites, factors [5,4,4]): the self-pay purchase write (pap_purchase_sale, user) and the modem usage-summary download (pap_compliance_download, agent) - disjoint events, tools and quantities. Blueprint constraint record: rental paid lines trigger a coverage charge whenever patient responsibility is not 0.00, pap_return triggers a resupply hold and pap_claim_reversal a coverage adjustment, so no tool of this difficulty writes those events; the numeric PAP writes left are sale, refund, service inspection/repair and compliance download, hence two problems per service call where the draw needs more problems than calls.
WHY A GOOD TEST. The patient asks only for the refund of a self-pay Auto-Adjusting CPAP she shipped back. The refund rule states three prerequisite sentences (state form) that wait on a return inspection on the device record carrying the used-accessory amount, the reconditioning parts amount and the reconditioning labor units; the records show only the delivery, a manufacturer-warranty repair and the completed return request, so the agent must discover the inspection, compute three quantities from three separate policies (each with its own ladders read from the device record, the return request, the delivery record and the patient's supply enrollment), record them in one inspection job, and only then compute the six-factor refund on the world that now carries the inspection. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling records and arithmetic, not from tool choice.
PROBLEM-TREE CARD. root pap_ext_self_pay_refund (target return_device_for_refund_b6f98fe9, owner user). Edges: (1) -> pap_ext_used_accessories, value_input, gate withheld_value, form state, sentence "The refund is fixed only after the device's service history carries a return inspection recording the value of used accessories the patient bears." (affirmative). (2) -> pap_ext_return_parts, value_input, gate restock_pct, form state, sentence "No restocking percentage is set on the refund until the return inspection on the device record shows the reconditioning parts amount." (negated). (3) -> pap_ext_return_labor, value_input, gate handling_charge, form state, "Before the refund's handling charge is applied, the return inspection on the device record must show the reconditioning labor units booked for the unit." (affirmative). All three resolve by record_return_inspection_bc7317cd (agent), the only write of this difficulty that puts a pap_repair job with repair_coverage none on a device record (state-form legality: exactly one write brings the state about). Four-point test: each joins the refund's own result to a record-visible state with only after / not ... until / before; names no tool, id or code token; strength is a hard wait, scope is the one inspection on this device. Opening evidence the state is false: initial_state.pap_service holds only 5737bff8 (pap_delivery) and 001e6f87 (pap_repair, repair_coverage manufacturer_warranty), no job with repair_coverage none. Topological order: the inspection call (step 8, resolves LABOR, PARTS, SHARE together, no edges among them) before the refund call (step 10). Parallel edges: the three prerequisite problems are resolved by one call, so no ordering choice exists. Edge deletion sensitivity (skip step 8, replay): refund 638.40 -> 706.09 (restock at the class 15 percent = 134.31 under the 140.00 cap, the standard kit 104.00 withheld because no used-accessory amount is recorded, handling 0.00 - a figure the refund rule's prerequisite sentences forbid fixing).
FACTOR CARD (handling-time world). LABOR result 8 (baseline 2): keep_time_units kept 15 days (delivery 2026-09-24 -> received 2026-10-09) -> 2 units [baseline 0 -> 6]; humidifier_care_units humidifier_included true and resupply 2b6df583 humidifier_in_use true -> 2 [cross-difficulty; -> 6]; setup_route_units delivery_mode virtual_setup (shipped) -> 1 [-> 7]; warranty_rework_protocol (method) one warranty job 001e6f87 with 1 labor unit -> sum 7 plus max(1, 1) [as counted -> 7]. PARTS result 56.00 (baseline 25.50 = filter set 7.50 + full air-path kit 18.00 by the delivery-date count): chamber_part_price 24.00 [-> 32.00]; outlet_part_price heated tubing on the active enrollment 12.00 [-> 44.00]; case_seal_part one manufacturer-warranty repair 001e6f87 -> 3.50 [-> 52.50]; airpath_clock_anchor (method) warranty repair 2026-09-30 is the start of the air-path count, 9 days to receipt -> half kit 9.00; near miss: the delivery-date count (15 days) or the transaction-date count for a shipped unit (22 days, from the sale line's adjudication_date 2026-09-17) would select the 18.00 kit [-> 65.00]. SHARE result 146.00 (baseline 104.00): mask_style_value full_face 129.00 [-> 106.00]; air_path_set_value heated + humidifier 63.00 [-> 138.00]; hygiene_charge_basis (method) active enrollment and 15 days -> mask 129.00 + 63.00 x 15/90 = 139.50 [full kit 192.00 -> 198.50]; travel_packaging_value shipped virtual-setup unit 6.50 [-> 139.50]. REFUND result 638.40 (baseline 660.15): wear_proration (method) 15 days -> 899.00 less 0.4 percent per day beyond 14 = 895.40 [-> 642.00]; restock_rate_tier recorded parts 56.00 >= 40.00 -> class 15 + 5 = 20 percent, raw 179.08 [-> 644.09]; restock_loyalty_cap (multi-source, cross-difficulty resupply) active enrollment open since 2024-03-12 (31 months) -> cap 140.00 [-> 599.32]; accessory_withholding recorded 146.00 above the 104.00 kit -> 146.00 [-> 680.40]; handling_charge_tier 8 labor units -> 20.00 [-> 658.40]; delivery_fee_credit (multi-source) warranty repair on record and shipped virtual-setup delivery -> 49.00 [-> 589.40]. Refund = 895.40 - 140.00 - 146.00 - 20.00 + 49.00 = 638.40.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD. pap_repair_responsibility.device_with_patient: status patient_owned on f9888c73 at the inspection (holds). pap_self_pay.return_window (time): anchor pap_holdings.setup_date 2026-09-24, 30 calendar days counted from the day after delivery, boundary included -> last day 2026-10-24; frozen 2026-10-14 is inside; 2026-10-25 would fail. pap_self_pay.refund_once: no pap_purchase_refund row names 4d775215 as original_bill_id at the opening. Overwrites: refund amount clause of pap_self_pay superseded (declared); "an owned self-pay device is repaired at the patient's cost (repair_coverage patient_paid)" and the warranty sentence of pap_repair_responsibility superseded by the inspection-not-repair sentence (both declared on pap_ext_used_accessories) so the inspection writes repair_coverage none and fires no coverage charge.
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Object: self-pay device record f9888c73 and its sale line 4d775215 (899.00 + 49.00 delivery, paid at order 2026-09-17). Receipt evidence: return_pickup request fcd0afb9 completed, decision_date 2026-10-09. The warranty job 001e6f87 is excluded from the inspection aggregates by repair_coverage manufacturer_warranty and is the evidence of the warranty factors.
PERSONA. Brisk retired librarian; volunteers only the refund request and the fact the branch has the unit; phone for lookup, DOB and ZIP on request; usage and the early power-brick swap only when asked; agrees to anything recorded first; runs the user tool with the stated amount; asks once mildly if the amount is below the price; no other ask. No prerequisite is named.
STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate by phone, verify by DOB + ZIP, read device, billing, service, requests and supply enrollment; compute LABOR 8, PARTS 56.00, SHARE 146.00 on the opening world; unlock and call the inspection tool; compute the refund 638.40 on the world carrying the inspection; unlock the user refund tool and hand it over with original_bill_id 4d775215, received_date 2026-10-09.
VERIFICATION (round 2, /tmp/pap_therapy_rentals_0057/verify.py, check_compute primitives on the handling-time worlds): LABOR 8 (factor baselines 6,6,7,7; all-baseline 2), PARTS 56.0 (32.0, 44.0, 52.5, 65.0; 25.5), SHARE 146.0 (106.0, 138.0, 198.5, 139.5; 104.0), REFUND 638.4 (642.0, 644.09, 599.32, 680.4, 658.4, 589.4; 660.15); skip step 8 -> REFUND 706.09.
DRAFT FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. Reading only the published rules, schemas and finder returns: the refund rule's sentences point at an inspection that is absent; the inspection policies give 8 units, 56.00 and 146.00 from the delivery, warranty job, return request and enrollment rows; the refund rule then gives 638.40 - agrees with gold.
ROUND 2 (policy-task audit rework). G3: wear_proration's top tier was a straight-line value that rose after day 21; replaced by a two-rate proration (0.4 percent per day for days 15-21, 0.8 percent per day beyond) - monotone, the refund only falls with days kept; this world (15 days) is unchanged at 895.40. Class sweep: restock tiers became additive (+5 / +2.5 points over the class percentage) so they never equal the class percentage of the 20-percent classes; accessory_withholding's tiers now all read the inspection (above the kit -> as recorded, sealed -> 0, otherwise -> kit minimum; see ROUND 3 for the no-inspection case), so no tier contradicts the refund's prerequisite sentence; warranty_rework_protocol tiers became sum + all warranty units + 2 / sum + max(1, units) / sum, distinct for every recorded unit count; hygiene_charge_basis (O2) became mask + tubing prorated over its 90-day replacement period, distinct from the full kit for every kept-day count inside the 30-day window (SHARE 186.50 -> 146.00, REFUND 597.90 -> 638.40, skip figure then 810.09, corrected in ROUND 3 to 706.09). O1: baseline wording 'the delivery fee is not refunded' -> 'the standard refund does not include the delivery fee'; 'the patient bears the mask value plus the tubing value' -> 'the standard used-accessory amount is ...'. O5: tenure reads the active enrollment. O6: outlet sentence names the active enrollment. O8: the warranty sentence of pap_repair_responsibility is declared superseded for the return inspection. Persona: the accessories used are the ones that came in the box, matching the rule.
ROUND 3 (policy-task audit revision_2). N1: the refund compute withheld 0.00 when no inspection was on the record (its zero test caught the no-inspection world), while the rule and baseline withhold the standard kit. The sealed tier now requires an inspection on the record (inspections >= 1 and recorded share 0), and the rule's fall-through tier names 'an amount above zero up to the standard kit or no used-accessory amount recorded on the device record' -> standard kit 104.00; opening-world / skip figure 810.09 -> 706.09 everywhere (edge_load_bearing, problem-tree card, verification). The scored 638.40 is unchanged. Class sweep, every compute branch against a stated tier or baseline sentence: usage_hours now states that a record with no scored window states 0.0 hours (its MX(1, count) guard); home_unit_purchase's no-wear tier now names 'or no usage summary is on the device record'; all other branches (parts air-path anchors, nights first-unit share with no window, refund cap with no active enrollment, labor min-1 unit) were already stated. Override sweep: N2 - home_unit_purchase now declares the superseded base pap_evt_rental_billing sentence 'A rental month is billed only while the device record is trial_active or rental_active.' (replaced by the same condition plus 'carries no self-pay sale of the unit'; pap_evt_rental_billing added to base_policy_refs), and states that the sale line is the patient's record of owning the unit while the device record keeps its status and coverage (O9 remainder). O8 remainder: used_accessories declares the superseded lead-in 'A repair is recorded only on a device the patient still has: ...' replaced by 'A return inspection is recorded on the device record of a self-pay unit that has come back to Summit Ridge while that record is patient_owned; it is not a repair of a device the patient still has.' (Round 4 narrowed this overwrite to the lead-in phrase only, so the base eligibility device_with_patient stays in force for the inspection and the solvability entry citing it is required; the record is patient_owned.)
ROUND 4 (render source mismatches r1). Item 1: the air-path kit factor's tiers rested on the day count another factor (airpath_clock_anchor) decided. Now the air-path kit by delivery-date days is part of the baseline (computation document), airpath_clock_anchor (method) decides the kit itself by moving the start of the count (latest warranty repair / transaction date on the sale line for a shipped unit / delivery date), and a new record-based parameter factor case_seal_part (tamper seals and case screws after warranty work: 7.00 / 3.50 / 0 by the warranty jobs on the device record) keeps four factors. PARTS 52.50 -> 56.00 (baseline 7.50 -> 25.50); the refund still takes the parts >= 40.00 tier, so it stays 638.40 and every refund sensitivity is unchanged. Items 2a-2c: the three pap_repair_responsibility overwrites on used_accessories now name their own scope ('For a self-pay device sent back for a refund, ... and only for such a device ...; every other ... remains ... as the base repair rule states'), and the device_with_patient lead-in overwrite now supersedes only 'A repair is recorded only on a device the patient still has', so the base state gate stays in force (the inspection meets it: patient_owned). Item 3 (minor, task 1 policies): swap credits read their own swap-job count. Item 4 (minor): the refund tool docstring no longer claims the card.
ROUND 5 (policy-task audit revision_4). N3: the refund tool docstring said 'The device price is the only amount refunded through this line', which reads the delivery-fee credit out of refund_amount (589.40 instead of 638.40); the sentence is removed, and the docstring now states only that one refund line carries the amount refunded to the patient and the received date. Class sweep of all four docstrings against their rules and bodies: the inspection docstring drops 'no fault', 'no loaner is issued' and 'nothing is billed to any insurance' (effects the rule does not state) and the '0.00 when the patient bears none' note on the used-accessory amount (the used-accessory rule never yields 0.00); the purchase docstring now calls sale_amount 'the sale amount charged to the patient for the unit' instead of 'the device price charged', because the rule's sale amount includes the humidifier amount. O12: the folded-line hyphen artefacts ('trial- compliance', 'coverage- billed', 'self- pay') in the overwrite replacement texts are rejoined; every replaced_by is now verbatim (space-normalized) in its rule. No figure moved: 8 / 56.00 / 146.00 / 638.40, skip 706.09.
ROUND 6 (KB audit source notes). S1: the air-path rule, its compute_basis and its factor ladder now name the field the compute reads - 'the transaction date on its sale line, the date the sale was paid and the unit left the warehouse' (pap_billing.adjudication_date, the schema's transaction date of a sale) - and the purchase tool's Returns now calls service_from_date 'the delivery date booked on the sale line, which for a unit already in the home is the day of the sale', so 'sale date' no longer names two fields; in this world the branch is not taken (a warranty repair decides the start). S2: the refund rule now states, scoped to the refunds it governs, that the restocking percentage is taken of the refundable value rather than of the full device price, and that the otherwise non-refundable delivery fee comes back only through the delivery fee credit - the two parameter descriptions of the base (not rule sentences) no longer give a second reading. S3 class sweep: the depended-on inspection rules no longer name the refund that waits on them - 'comes back to Summit Ridge for a refund' / 'sent back for a refund' became 'on a completed return pickup request' in the labor rule, the used-accessory rule and its three scoped overwrite replacements; the refund's dependency is carried only by its three prerequisite sentences. No figure moved: 8 / 56.00 / 146.00 / 638.40, skip 706.09.
user_scenario:
You are Doreen Kowalczyk, a 70-year-old retired school librarian in Pittsburgh who speaks politely, a little briskly, and likes to get to the point. Back in September you bought an auto-adjusting CPAP machine outright from Summit Ridge Home Medical and paid for it on your card, hoping it would be gentler than your old machine. It was shipped to your house and a Summit Ridge therapist walked you through the setup on a video call, but it never really suited you, so you packed it back into its original box and shipped it back with the return label the branch sent you. The branch let you know it arrived last week. You are calling today, inside the thirty days, because you want your refund for that machine processed now, back onto the card you paid with. You start the call by saying exactly that: "I sent back the auto CPAP I bought from you in September, the branch has it, and I'd like my refund put through today, back on my card."

To find you, you give your phone number when asked for something to look you up by: 4125550137. If the agent needs to confirm who you are, you give your date of birth, July 19, 1956 (1956-07-19), and your home ZIP code, 15237, one at a time as they ask. You do not know any account or reference numbers and say so if asked; you assume they can see your purchase.

If the agent asks how you used the machine, you say you used it most nights for about two weeks, with the full face mask and heated hose that came in the box (the same kind you get from your supply subscription), before you gave up on it. If asked whether anything went wrong with it, you remember the power brick died in the first week and Summit Ridge swapped it for you, but you do not volunteer this otherwise. You do not know what Summit Ridge does with a returned machine and you never suggest any step to the agent.

You are happy for the agent to take care of whatever has to be recorded on their side; if they tell you something needs to be done first, you say that is fine and to go ahead. When the agent tells you the refund amount and hands you the refund confirmation to complete yourself, you complete it with the amount they gave you. If the amount is lower than what you paid, you ask once, in a mild tone, why it isn't the full price, and you accept whatever explanation the agent gives; you never name a figure of your own. Once the agent tells you the refund has gone through, you thank them and end the call. You do not ask for anything else.
